questions.question_text: Which of the following statistical procedures involve strati�ed analysis of odds ratio in the presence of confounding?
questions.explanation:
The Mantel-Haenszel technique is an excellent method for adjusting for confounding factors when analysing the relationship between a
dichotomous outcome and a dichotomous risk factor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods is NOT used to minimise confounding factors in a case-control study?
questions.explanation:
Randomisation, restriction and matching are three methods that can be used while designing a study to control for confounders.

questions.question_text:
Various study designs can be used to investigate causality. In such investigations, the most important di�erence between an experimental
study and an observational study is that

options.text: The researcher controls the exposure of the subjects in an experimental study
The study and control groups are selected according to exposure status in an experimental study
The experimental study needs ethical approval
The study and control groups are carefully matched in an experimental study

correct_answer.text: The researcher controls the exposure of the subjects in an experimental study

questions.explanation:
In experimental studies, the exposure of the subjects to a putative causal factor / treatment factor is controlled by the researcher. Both
types of studies need ethical approval. Cohort studies are observational and still prospective. Matching two groups is necessary for both
types of studies. This can be achieved by randomization in experiments.

questions.question_text:
While conducting a study, all enrolled subjects were matched for age, gender, smoking and body mass index before studying to control for
confounding. Which of the following type of studies is most suitable for the above method?

options.text: A cross-sectional study design to study interaction between multiple social and environmental variables on adolescent depression

A prospective cohort study of 1684 subjects.
A case control study requiring a total sample size of 30 each.
A randomised control trial evaluating the e�ect of Bupropion on smoking cessation.

correct_answer.text: A case control study requiring a total sample size of 30 each.

questions.explanation:
Matching is possible for smaller studies. It is not needed for RCTs and extremely di�cult for large cohort studies. It is not possible for
ecological studies and cross-sectional surveys.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a criterion used in assessing the evidence for causality in medical research?
questions.explanation:
Hill's criteria for causality includes consistency, speci�city, temporality and biological gradient (dose-response relationship). Consistency

populations and using di�erent methods. If a speci�c exposure can be isolated from others and associated with a speci�c disease, then such
speci�city supports causality. This is perhaps the most di�cult criterion to ful�ll because in practice many exposures (e.g., cigarettes or
radiation) are associated with multiple e�ects and speci�c diseases often have more than one cause. Temporality refers to time relationship
between cause and e�ect: the factor believed to have caused the disease must have occurred prior to disease development. Hill AB: The
environment and disease: Association or causation? Proc R Soc Med 58:295-330, 1965

questions.question_text:
An observed dose-response e�ect supports the hypothesis of a causal relationship, according to Hill's criteria. But many well-designed
studies of a genuinely causal relationship may fail to show a dose-response e�ect. Which is the least likely explanation for such results?

options.text: All doses are too low to reveal the e�ect
There is no real dose-response e�ect
All doses are too high to reveal the e�ect

correct_answer.text: There is no real dose-response e�ect

questions.explanation:
If a dose-response relationship is present, it provides a strong evidence for a causal relationship. However, the absence of a dose-response
relationship does not necessarily rule out a causal relationship. In some cases in which a threshold may exist, no disease may develop up to
a certain level of exposure; above this threshold level, the disease may manifest. The study might have included only below threshold
exposures; similarly if there is a dose window only within which the response occurs, again this may be missed if all participants are outside
the window. Similarly confounders and random variation may obscure the association.

questions.question_text:
A researcher is interested in the e�ects of alcohol use on REM sleep architecture. But she is aware that cannabis or nicotine use is a
potential extraneous variable; so she picks only those subjects who do not use cannabis or nicotine before determining their alcohol status.

questions.explanation:
The study has been restricted to a population group lacking the confounding factor, namely exposure to cannabis or nicotine. This is known
